hypotheses.claim: Under the muṣḥaf-spiral placement, āyāt sharing a rare root lie closer in direction than random pairs — including across sūrahs — while the legacy برج placement shows no such locality.
Lexical continuity across an isnād seam (the stitch half of رِباط = √(continuity × delta)) exceeds the continuity across an arbitrary non-seam point in the same sūrah.
The last three āyāt of a sūrah sit nearer to direct address (lower discourse distance) than the sūrah's own average.
A seeded voyage (evidence-weighted, with memory) visits more distinct sūrahs and revisits fewer āyāt in 40 legs than a uniform random walk over the same relations.
At this field's scale, the floating origin is needed to keep vertex quantisation below visibility.
Āyāt with no person mass are not spread evenly over the muṣḥaf; they concentrate in particular sūrahs beyond what sūrah length explains.
